blocks.p: Most of Bunyan’s names still say exactly what they mean and are kept unchanged. These have been renamed because their meaning has worn away. The first group carries over from Part One; the last two are new in Part Two.

rows: Slough and despond are both unfamiliar now; the sense is a bog of despair
A by-end was a hidden, selfish motive
A pickthank was a flatterer who curried favor
The street where Talkative’s family lives; prating is idle chatter
Two of the twelve jurors at Vanity Fair
Christiana’s neighbor, kin to the Timid of Part One
Halt meant lame; he travels on crutches and is quick to stumble, not to stop
